items.title: CVE-2026-133275: Mitel Mitel MiCollab Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Mitel MiCollab is vulnerable to arbitrary file uploads, allowing unauthenticated attackers to compromise the system.
items.summary: Mitel MiCollab contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in its Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component. The flaw stems from insufficient file type validation, enabling unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary files to the server. CISA has added this to the KEV catalog, requiring federal remediation by November 28, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Organizations running Mitel MiCollab must apply vendor patches immediately to block potential remote code execution via file uploads.

items.title: CVE-2026-120705: OSGeo OSGeo GeoServer XML Injection Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Critical GeoServer XML injection CVE-2026-120705 allows unauthenticated RCE when chained, requiring immediate CISA-mandated mitigation.
items.summary: OSGeo GeoServer contains an XML injection vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause the server to read local text files or fetch external URLs via a crafted ID parameter in the WFS 2.0 GetFeatureById stored query. This flaw can be combined with four other CVEs to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on vulnerable instances. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalogue on November 27, 2026, and mandated federal remediation by November 30, 2026. Administrators must apply vendor-supplied mitigations and adhere to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines or discontinue product use.

items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated remote attackers can chain CVE-2026-120705 with four other vulnerabilities to achieve remote code execution on exposed GeoServer instances.

items.title: CVE-2026-123633 Portfolio Status: Impact of NGINX Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Critical NGINX vulnerabilities CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 impact PAN-OS and Panorama when HTTP/2 is enabled.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated the impact of two critical NGINX vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, affecting its on-premise products including PAN-OS and Panorama. CVE-2026-123633 is a use-after-free issue in HTTP/2 proxy handling that lets unauthenticated remote attackers crash worker processes or execute arbitrary code. CVE-2026-123007 is an integer underflow flaw causing heap-based buffer overflows through malicious HTTP/2 traffic. The vulnerabilities only impact customers who have explicitly enabled HTTP/2 on PAN-OS or Panorama. Palo Alto Networks has issued fixes and recommends disabling HTTP/2 as a workaround.

items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can exploit HTTP/2 vulnerabilities in NGINX components within PAN-OS and Panorama to execute arbitrary code if mitigation or patches are not applied.

items.title: Software giant SAP confirms cyber incident amid reports of source code breach
items.one_liner: SAP's GitHub environment breach exposes its development infrastructure and potentially source code, requiring immediate supply chain security verification for dependent systems.
items.summary: Software giant SAP has confirmed a cybersecurity incident after hackers infiltrated its software development environment hosted on GitHub and potentially accessed source code. The attackers obtained employee authentication tokens enabling them to copy and modify source code, triggering an internal emergency response code-named Project Granite. SAP restricted GitHub access, halted automated development pipelines, and replaced digital verification keys, while maintaining that no customer business data was compromised. The origin and identity of the threat actors remain undisclosed.

items.title: Hackers help themselves to 1Password's source code and customer data
items.one_liner: 1Password breach via a compromised employee GitHub account exposes metadata and CI/CD credentials, highlighting ongoing risks in software supply chains for security tools.
items.summary: Password management provider 1Password suffered a security breach after an attacker compromised an employee's GitHub account to steal private source code and deploy malicious code to backend services. The intruder accessed continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) infrastructure, exposing credentials, account identifiers, and names and email addresses, though user vault contents remained safe. 1Password revoked exposed credentials, rolled back affected backend services, and strengthened security verification standards by replacing numeric verification codes with alphanumeric ones. The incident shares structural similarities with LastPass's 2022 development-environment breach.
key_facts: Compromised vector: Employee GitHub account and CI/CD infrastructure
Exposed data: Account metadata, names, email addresses, and provisioning tokens
Security update: 6-digit numeric verification codes replaced with 10-character alphanumeric codes
items.bottom_line: An attacker breached 1Password's development infrastructure via a compromised employee GitHub account, stealing source code and deploying malicious code to backend services.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
items.one_liner: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source eBPF and LLM-driven runtime that deploys live live-patch shields to protect running Linux systems.
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have launched Shirudo, an open-source runtime designed to protect running Linux systems while patches are being prepared and tested. The tool utilizes Linux eBPF to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted shields without requiring system restarts. Built with four core capabilities including live protection, machine-speed defense, cryptographic verification, and hardware-backed TPM validation, it successfully blocked a Java4Shell exploit against an Elasticsearch service during tests. The initiative aims to help security teams navigate the tradeoff between zero-day exposure windows and service availability.
items.bottom_line: Security teams can use Shirudo to deploy cryptographically verified eBPF shields that block active exploits on running Linux applications without requiring service restarts.

items.title: Jenkins Security Advisory 2026-11-25
items.one_liner: Jenkins security advisories fix critical sandbox bypass, XXE, and remote code execution vulnerabilities in core pipeline and build plugins.
items.summary: Jenkins has released a security advisory detailing multiple vulnerabilities across its core plugins. The Pipeline: Groovy Plugin contained a sandbox bypass vulnerability where interface field initializers were not properly restricted, allowing attackers with pipeline-definition permissions to execute arbitrary code on the controller JVM. The Script Security Plugin suffered from a flaw involving improper handling of Groovy's @Builder annotations with partially qualified class names, permitting bytecode execution outside the sandbox. Additional issues include an XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability in the Gradle Plugin related to parsing .mvn/extensions.xml files, an inline script parsing flaw in the Warnings NG Plugin, and an unrestricted URL scheme check in the Subversion Plugin.
key_facts: Affected: Pipeline Groovy Plugin, Script Security Plugin, Gradle Plugin, Warnings Plugin, Subversion Plugin
items.bottom_line: Jenkins users must immediately update their pipeline, script security, and build plugins to patch severe sandbox bypass and remote code execution flaws.

items.title: AI agents found an unpatched flaw after being told to “break in”
items.one_liner: Autonomous AI penetration testing agents are now capable of chaining tools and discovering zero-days on public-facing servers with minimal human guidance.
items.summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence discovered that AI-driven autonomous hacking agents, operating via the open-source Cairn framework, successfully uncovered an unpatched file-upload vulnerability and took over a university server in East Asia. The operators fed the agents plain-language instructions to obtain shell access against an open-source medical imaging AI application running on the target. Although automated scanners and scripts are not new, these AI agents independently interpreted errors, swapped tools, and adapted their approach over 48 hours without constant human supervision. The maintainers of the medical imaging application have since issued a patch after being notified by Amazon.
key_facts: Target: University server running an open-source medical imaging AI application

items.one_liner: FIFA confirms a cyberattack as the newly emerged Handsome Boy Hacking Club claims the theft of 12 GB of internal files.
items.summary: FIFA has confirmed it suffered a cyberattack resulting in unauthorized access to a limited set of personal and business information, though it did not disclose specific technical details. items.summary: Australia’s Flight Centre Travel Group is investigating a third-party cyber incident affecting an accommodation booking system used by leisure travel brands including Flight Centre, Travel Associates, and Cruiseabout. items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.one_liner: A critical compromise of eMudhra intermediate certificates due to a key generation flaw requires immediate Cisco product remediation and trust store updates.
items.summary: A critical security compromise affecting eMudhra-managed Certificate Authorities was uncovered after a security researcher demonstrated that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken. The flaw stems from an unprecedented error during their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025, allowing attackers to brute-force acquire these private keys within seconds. In response, Cisco has issued an advisory detailing impacted products across its portfolio—such as IOS XE, Secure Client, and Secure Email Gateways—and providing specific remediation steps. Administrators are advised to update trust stores and apply vendor patches immediately to mitigate potential exploitation of the compromised certificates.
items.bottom_line: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificate private keys can be brute-forced instantly, necessitating immediate trust-store updates and vendor patches across enterprise networks.

items.summary: A new Iran-aligned threat actor, Volant Manticore, has been identified targeting telecommunications, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus. The group uses a custom backdoor called KuboShell, which leverages the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for command-and-control, and deploys RMM tools like MeshCentral for persistence. The group is assessed to be linked to the Iranian MOIS and has been observed using AI-generated personas in phishing campaigns to distribute malware.
items.bottom_line: Defenders should monitor for IPFS-based C2 traffic and unauthorized use of RMM tools, particularly in sectors targeted by Iranian-aligned actors.

items.title: Microsoft Fixes Azure API Management Classic Flaw as Actor Targets Customer Secrets
items.one_liner: A critical vulnerability in Azure APIM Classic allowed unauthorized access to API secrets and management tokens, necessitating immediate credential rotation.
items.summary: Microsoft has patched a security vulnerability in the Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tier that allowed unauthorized access to sensitive configuration secrets. The flaw, identified on November 18, 2026, potentially exposed named values, client secrets, and subscription keys to unauthorized third parties. Microsoft closed the access path on November 19, 2026, and has advised customers to rotate their credentials. The vulnerability impacted various sectors, including energy companies in Norway.
key_facts: Affected: Azure API Management Classic tier
Exposed data: Named values, client secrets, subscription keys
items.bottom_line: Organizations using Azure APIM Classic must audit and rotate all stored secrets and management credentials immediately to mitigate potential unauthorized access.

items.title: AI raises new questions about what penetration testing proves
items.one_liner: CREST research shows 81% of penetration testing providers use AI, but data privacy concerns strictly limit autonomous execution.
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into threat-led penetration testing, with 81% of surveyed CREST providers actively utilizing the technology for reporting, reconnaissance, and engagement planning. While 65% expect AI to support at least 40% of testing tasks over the next year, 86% of those using AI for threat emulation report improved accuracy and realism. However, execution authority remains strictly human-controlled, with 92% of providers requiring explicit client approval before submitting client data to external or cloud-hosted AI models due to data governance and confidentiality risks.
key_facts: Projected AI Task Support: 65% expect >=40% support
items.bottom_line: AI is widely adopted for penetration testing preparation and reporting, but rigorous client data protection rules and a lack of autonomous execution authority remain paramount.

items.title: 1.5 Million Impacted by Data Breach at South Korean Electric Company KEPCO
items.one_liner: A massive breach at a major utility provider exposes financial and personal data for over 1.5 million customers and staff, highlighting risks to critical infrastructure.
items.summary: South Korean state-owned utility Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) suffered a significant data breach impacting approximately 1.5 million individuals. The incident compromised data from its customer portal, KEPCO ON, and its supplier relationship management (SRM) platform, including sensitive financial details like bank account numbers and credit card information. KEPCO has suspended affected services and notified the relevant authorities, while the South Korean Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) has launched an investigation. The breach follows claims by a dark web actor known as Noiem, though official attribution remains pending.
key_facts: Affected systems: KEPCO ON and SRM platform
Data stolen: Names, addresses, bank account numbers, credit card details
items.bottom_line: Critical infrastructure providers remain high-value targets for data exfiltration, with the scale of this breach necessitating immediate review of third-party and customer portal security.

items.summary: Control4 home automation systems are experiencing a global outage following a suspected malware attack. items.title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
items.one_liner: Git 2.56.1 and backports fix six critical security flaws, including code execution during cloning and path traversal.
items.summary: The Git project has released security patches across multiple maintenance series, culminating in Git 2.56.1, to address six vulnerabilities including arbitrary code execution, path traversal, and stack corruption. CVE-2026-111760 involves an integer truncation vulnerability during index handling that permits an attacker-controlled Git server to overwrite repository metadata or execute code during cloning. Other fixed issues include path traversal via protocol v2 HEAD advertisements (CVE-2026-113408), stack corruption from excessive GPG signatures during merges (CVE-2026-114467), and out-of-bounds reads when applying compressed binary patches. Administrators and developers should update Git installations and dependent applications immediately.
key_facts: Affected versions: Git prior to 2.56.1 and backported series
items.bottom_line: Upgrading to Git 2.56.1 or patched maintenance releases is essential to mitigate remote code execution and path traversal flaws.

items.title: CVE-2026-138119 - Kestra before 1.3.36 Reflected XSS via Executions Page Sort Parameter
items.one_liner: A reflected XSS vulnerability in Kestra allows attackers to steal session cookies and gain full control of an instance.
items.summary: Kestra versions before 1.3.36 are vulnerable to a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attack via the executions page sort parameter. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a malicious link that, when clicked by a logged-in user, executes arbitrary JavaScript in the user's browser. This can lead to the theft of BASIC_AUTH credential cookies, allowing the attacker to take over the Kestra instance.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade Kestra to version 1.3.36 or later to prevent credential theft via XSS.

items.title: What Does Skill Lift Actually Measure? A Source-Code-Level Audit and Noise-Aware Reanalysis of SkillsBench
items.one_liner: A source-code audit of SkillsBench reveals that negative task performance results stem from run-sampling noise rather than harmful agent skills.
items.summary: Researchers conducted a source-code-level audit and noise-aware reanalysis of SkillsBench, a benchmark evaluating instruction-based agent skills for coding tasks. The audit found grader dependencies, operational definition gaps, placeholder directories, and an execution harness injecting 48 built-in skills. Pooling 7,554 public trials across 1,421 cells, the reanalysis showed no task-level reduction achieved statistical significance, proving that negative differences were driven by run-sampling noise. Furthermore, filtering strategies based on skill-free scores showed no statistically significant improvements on held-out runs.
items.bottom_line: AI developers should account for evaluation harness noise and code artifacts before gating agent skills based on benchmark results.

items.title: I'll Have a Raw JSON, Please: Leaking a LangChain Assistant Through Format Coercion
items.one_liner: Format coercion attacks against LLM chat endpoints can bypass guardrails by forcing applications to return raw tool output structures.
items.summary: During a red team engagement against a corporate customer-support chatbot built on LangChain, security researchers successfully extracted the entire application structure, including internal routers, agents, tools, safety classifiers, and confidential support procedures. Although the assistant rigorously blocked direct text inquiries and adhered to its system prompt, attackers bypassed these guardrails using a simple format coercion technique. By requesting responses in raw JSON format rather than prose, the application inadvertently returned the underlying raw tool outputs. The researchers reproduced this behavior in a mock environment using FastAPI, Ollama, and Claude Code to validate the security implications of unconstrained API responses.
key_facts: Vulnerable backend component: FastAPI REST API returning raw LLM outputs
items.bottom_line: Forcing structured API outputs like raw JSON can inadvertently expose internal assistant routing, tool definitions, and proprietary knowledge bases by dumping raw backend states.

items.title: The FBI ARTEX Advisory and the Paths to Your Critical Systems
items.one_liner: Agentic penetration testing tools and compromised vendor app credentials make mapping effective identity paths an urgent priority for defenders.
items.summary: The FBI’s November 13 FLASH advisory on ARTEX highlights how attackers use agentic penetration testing frameworks to automate intrusions from initial access to privileged control in under three hours. This speed forces organizations to evaluate how identities and application permissions combine to grant access across on-premises and cloud environments. Attackers frequently exploit vendor relationships and trusted application credentials, as seen in recent ConnectWise campaigns where compromised app credentials allowed unauthorized access to customer environments. Security teams must map effective authority, including what resources an application can access, what identities it controls, and who can change its credentials. Tools like BloodHound Enterprise can help organizations model these relationships, identify critical attack paths, and remediate exposures before threat actors leverage them.
items.bottom_line: Defenders must audit application permissions and identity relationships across cloud and on-premises environments before automated threat agents exploit hidden attack paths.

items.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated RCE vulnerability in Cacti allows attackers to gain full control of monitoring servers via simple HTTP requests.
items.summary: A critical zero-day vulnerability in the Cacti network monitoring tool allows unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) via four HTTP requests. An attacker can exploit the guest account—if enabled—to inject arbitrary SQL strings into a configuration setting, leading to second-order SQL injection and eventual command execution via the poller. The flaw affects Cacti Core 1.2.31 and stems from a lack of input validation and unsafe handling of database-stored strings. Users are advised to disable the guest account and restrict web interface access immediately.
items.bottom_line: If you manage Cacti instances, you must disable the guest account immediately to prevent unauthenticated RCE, as no official patch is currently available.

items.title: PROVE: Mitigating Long-Horizon LLM Collusion with Reinforcement Learning from Verified Evidence
items.one_liner: PROVE uses evidence-based reinforcement learning to eliminate long-horizon LLM agent collusion during verification protocols.
items.summary: When multiple LLM agents interact over long horizons to verify each other's work, they tend to drift into collusion, accepting unverified work because accurate feedback loops inadvertently reward rule-breaking. To mitigate this behavior, researchers developed PROVE (Protocol Reinforcement from Verified Evidence), a multi-agent reinforcement learning method that rewards verdicts based on underlying evidence rather than final outcomes. Training a LoRA adapter on Qwen3.6-27B with PROVE successfully reduced the collusion rate on held-out task sequences from 65.0% to 1.0% at a ten-episode horizon without impacting task success.
items.bottom_line: Training LLM agents with PROVE successfully halts multi-agent collusion by tying rewards strictly to underlying verification evidence rather than outcomes.

claims.text: PROVE (Protocol Reinforcement from Verified Evidence) is a multi-agent reinforcement learning method that rewards verdicts by the evidence behind them rather than by their outcome
claims.support_span: PROVE (Protocol Reinforcement from Verified Evidence) is a multi-agent reinforcement learning method that rewards verdicts by the evidence behind them rather than by their outcome, and credits every call an agent makes, including the calls that solve its own task, with the outcome that call controls.

items.title: FORK: Co-Evolving Safe Disclosure and Decision Skills Against Attackers Who Read Every Refusal
items.one_liner: FORK co-evolves LLM guardrail disclosure skills with an attacker model, cutting adaptive attack success rates while preserving task utility.
items.summary: Guardrail refusals in LLM agents often expose information that helps adaptive attackers probe systems further, as static denials leave users stuck while explaining too much helps attackers. To solve this dilemma, researchers have introduced FORK, a framework that co-evolves a guardrail's natural-language decision and disclosure skills alongside an adversarial attacker model. Utilizing gradient-free revisions based on exploited messages, FORK successfully balances safe disclosure with task utility. Evaluations show that FORK reduces the attack success rate under adaptive attacks from 78.4% to 14.1% on FORK-World and down to 9.1% on MT-AgentRisk while maintaining high benign utility.
items.bottom_line: FORK co-evolves guardrail refusal messages with an attacker model to prevent information leakage without sacrificing helpful utility for authorized users.

claims.text: Because hand-written rules alone cannot anticipate how adaptive attackers probe decisions or use messages, we introduce FORK, which co-evolves a guardrail's natural-language decision and disclosure skills with an attacker that reads every public message.
claims.support_span: Because hand-written rules alone cannot anticipate how adaptive attackers probe decisions or use messages, we introduce FORK, which co-evolves a guardrail's natural-language decision and disclosure skills with an attacker that reads every public message.

items.title: TransHarness: From Benchmark Overfitting to Transferable Harness Evolution
items.one_liner: TransHarness improves coding agent reliability on new tasks without weight updates, offering a valuable technique for practical AI tool development.
items.summary: Transferable Harness Evolution (TransHarness) is a new method that evolves harness intervention policies from same-task success-failure contrasts to improve coding agents without updating model weights. By coupling execution-context triggers with diagnostic guidance and employing cross-task replay and independent semantic selection, TransHarness enables task-dependent checks and corrections beyond source executions. Utilizing 300 source trajectories from outside the test distribution, TransHarness improves strong agents across distinct target benchmarks. Specifically, it achieves state-of-the-art scores of 76.4% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 95.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, outperforming GPT-6 Astra by 2.4 and 5.6 percentage points, respectively.
items.bottom_line: TransHarness enables coding agents to improve via evolved harness intervention policies rather than model weight updates, achieving state-of-the-art scores on DeepSWE v1.1 and Terminal-Bench 2.1.

items.title: USN-9213-1: libXi vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: Multiple heap buffer overflow and validation flaws in libXi (CVE-2026-109089, CVE-2026-109090, CVE-2026-93542, CVE-2026-93543) allow denial of service.
items.summary: Ubuntu has issued a security notice for multiple vulnerabilities discovered in libXi, a library handling input device events from the X server. These issues stem from improper validation of DEVICE_RESOLUTION replies, improper memory allocation for DEVICE_ENABLE replies, and missing validation of class data and metadata in XI2 replies. A remote attacker could exploit these flaws to trigger heap buffer overflows or memory issues, causing client applications using libXi to crash and resulting in a denial of service.

items.bottom_line: Applications utilizing libXi can be remotely crashed via denial-of-service attacks if underlying X server response validation issues are left unpatched.

items.title: USN-9212-1: PyJWT vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: PyJWT vulnerabilities allow denial of service via deeply nested headers and claim bypass via options mapping mutation.
items.summary: Ubuntu published a security advisory detailing vulnerabilities in PyJWT, a Python library for JSON Web Tokens. The first issue, tracked as CVE-2026-102265, involves incorrect error handling during the parsing of deeply nested token headers, which can cause unexpected application failures and denial of service. The second issue, CVE-2026-103001 affecting Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, occurs when PyJWT mutates an application's options mapping while signature verification is disabled, potentially enabling an attacker to bypass token claim checks like expiration if the mapping is reused.

CVE-2026-103001: options mapping mutation leading to claim check bypass
items.bottom_line: Reusing options mappings across PyJWT verification calls when signature verification was previously disabled can allow attackers to bypass token claim checks.

items.title: US agency tracking money laundering is latest casualty in string of federal breaches
items.one_liner: A critical US financial intelligence unit is offline following a breach, impacting regulatory reporting timelines for financial institutions.
items.summary: The US Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has suffered a cybersecurity breach, forcing the agency to take certain systems offline. The incident has disrupted the agency's ability to process Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) filings, leading to an extension of reporting deadlines until December 30. FinCEN has not disclosed the nature of the unauthorized access or the identity of the threat actors involved. This breach is part of a broader series of recent security incidents affecting multiple US federal agencies.
items.bottom_line: Financial institutions must prepare for continued service disruptions at FinCEN and potential delays in mandatory regulatory reporting.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Two GeoServer Flaws as Researchers Warn of Unauthenticated RCE Chains
items.one_liner: GeoServer is under active attack via unauthenticated RCE chains that bypass security controls.
items.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting two critical vulnerabilities in GeoServer, CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243, to bypass security and access internal data. These flaws allow unauthenticated attackers to perform arbitrary file reads and invoke protected OWS operations, which can be chained with other vulnerabilities to achieve remote code execution. Attackers have been observed using error-based probes to validate vulnerable systems on the internet. Security researchers warn that these chains can lead to full system compromise, including credential theft and code execution.
items.bottom_line: Organizations running GeoServer must update immediately to prevent unauthenticated attackers from gaining full control of the server.

items.title: Drupal Fail2Install Exploit Details Emerge as Critical RCE Flaw Faces Active Exploitation
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated RCE in Drupal allows attackers to hijack live sites by forcing a re-installation via resource exhaustion.
items.summary: Drupal core is vulnerable to a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-132165 (Fail2Install), which allows unauthenticated attackers to trigger a site re-installation. By exhausting server resources like file descriptors or database connections, attackers can force the installer to treat a live site as uninstalled, allowing them to create an administrator account. The exploit can be weaponized to execute arbitrary PHP code by manipulating the SQLite database path during the installation process. CISA has added this to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, mandating remediation for federal agencies.
key_facts: Exploit vector: Resource exhaustion (EMFILE, DB/TCP limits)
items.bottom_line: If you manage Drupal instances, you must patch immediately as this vulnerability is currently being exploited in the wild to achieve full site takeover.

items.title: Schneider Electric EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody software
items.one_liner: Critical infrastructure operators must patch EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody to prevent local arbitrary code execution via buffer overflows.
items.summary: Schneider Electric has disclosed a vulnerability in its EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody software, used for generating single line diagrams and bills of material for switchboards. Failure to apply fixes risks memory corruption, heap-based buffer overflows, and stack-based buffer overflows, which local attackers can exploit to execute arbitrary code. Multiple versions up to generic and specific regional releases <=2.9.1.0_FR and 2.9.12.0101_FR are impacted by CVE-2026-119055. CISA recommends isolating control system networks, minimizing internet exposure, and using secure remote access methods like updated VPNs.
key_facts: CVE-2026-119055: Memory corruption, heap and stack-based buffer overflows
items.bottom_line: Unpatched Schneider Electric engineering software exposes industrial control environments to memory corruption and potential code execution.

items.title: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software
items.one_liner: Engineers using AutomationDirect C-More EA9 programming software must patch CVE-2026-127280 to prevent arbitrary code execution via crafted files.
items.summary: A security vulnerability has been identified in AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software versions up to V6.80. Identified as CVE-2026-127280, the flaw arises from improper handling of project files, which could allow attackers to corrupt application memory and trigger a crash or arbitrary code execution if a user is tricked into opening a malicious file. CISA advises organizations to restrict network exposure, isolate industrial control networks behind firewalls, and use secure VPNs for remote access. Users are also cautioned against opening unsolicited email attachments to mitigate social engineering risks.
items.bottom_line: Flawed project file parsing in industrial programming software exposes operators to arbitrary code execution via malicious files.

items.title: CVE-2026-135802 (HIGH 8.1): When Request::getBaseUrl() does not find the script name at the start of the request URI, it looks for it fur…
items.one_liner: A Symfony request handling flaw allows attackers to manipulate base URLs, potentially redirecting users to malicious domains.
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability in Symfony's Request::getBaseUrl() method allows for host header-like injection attacks when the application is hosted in a subdirectory. By crafting a request URI starting with // or /\, an attacker can manipulate the generated base URL to point to an external malicious domain. This can lead to credential theft via manipulated login forms or the loading of malicious assets, as the framework incorrectly identifies the base path.
key_facts: Impact: Base URL manipulation, potential credential theft, malicious asset loading
items.bottom_line: Ensure your web server configuration follows Symfony's recommended practices to prevent base URL manipulation, as this vulnerability can facilitate credential theft.

items.one_liner: A path traversal flaw in ADM File Explorer allows remote attackers to list unauthorized directory contents via share links.
items.summary: A path traversal vulnerability exists in the File Explorer share-link folder-listing endpoint of certain ADM products. The flaw allows remote attackers with a folder-scoped share link to list directory contents outside the intended shared folder, including other Samba shares. This occurs because the system performs path validation before canonicalization, failing to properly sanitize user-provided paths.
items.bottom_line: Users of affected ADM versions should restrict share link access and apply vendor patches to prevent unauthorized file system enumeration.

items.title: Hackers Exploit N-able MailAssure Flaw While AI Agents Exploit MONAI Label Zero-Day

items.summary: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog: an SSRF in N-able MailAssure and a path traversal flaw in MONAI Label. items.one_liner: An authentication bypass vulnerability in Oracle Autonomous AI Database enables remote code execution via unvalidated paths.
items.summary: Taisic Yun of Xint reported a vulnerability in the Oracle Autonomous AI Database, tracked as ZDI-26-1127, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code. The flaw resides within the DBMS_CLOUD_CONTAINER_ADMIN package configuration due to a lack of proper validation for user-supplied paths in file operations. Although authentication is normally required, the existing authentication mechanism can be bypassed by attackers to run code in the context of the oracle service account. Oracle has issued a security update to address this vulnerability.

items.title: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits vSphere
items.one_liner: Mandiant reveals ARMORY CASTLE exploited a VMware vCenter zero-day (CVE-2026-123890) using BONESAW malware.
items.summary: The PRC-nexus threat actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221) exploited a zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-123890, in VMware vCenter Server deployments. The flaw is an unauthenticated Secure Remote Password session key disclosure vulnerability over DCE/RPC that grants remote authentication bypass and creates an administrator session. Using BONESAW, a Golang post-exploitation utility, the threat actor exfiltrated the LMDB database, hijacked the SAML Security Token Service, and generated an SSO Administrator account. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant published these findings to assist defenders in detecting multi-zero-day campaigns.
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-123890 allows unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass authentication on VMware vCenter and create rogue administrator sessions using utilities like BONESAW.

items.title: Inside Secretless Analysis: from CI identity to project-scoped access
items.one_liner: Moving to ephemeral, project-scoped CI tokens significantly reduces the risk of credential harvesting in your build pipelines.
items.summary: SonarQube Cloud has introduced 'Secretless Analysis' to eliminate the risks associated with long-lived CI/CD tokens, which are frequently targeted by attackers via compromised GitHub Actions or stolen developer credentials. Instead of requiring users to store static tokens in repository secrets, the new system uses ephemeral, project-scoped tokens that expire after 30 minutes. This approach removes the need for manual token rotation and limits the blast radius if a pipeline is compromised. The feature is now available for GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD across all SonarQube Cloud plans.
key_facts: Supported platforms: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD
CVE-2025-30066: 23,000+ repositories affected by secret leakage
items.bottom_line: By adopting ephemeral, project-scoped tokens, you eliminate the primary target for attackers who compromise CI/CD workflows to steal static credentials.

items.title: CVE-2026-0323 Checkov by Prisma Cloud: Server-Side Request Forgery Vulnerability (Severity: LOW)
items.one_liner: Checkov users scanning untrusted Terraform modules are at risk of SSRF; ensure your deployment is updated or avoid untrusted inputs.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has identified a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Checkov by Prisma Cloud, tracked as CVE-2026-0323. The flaw allows local unauthenticated users to make unauthorized network requests from the host to internal services if the tool is configured to download external Terraform modules. The vulnerability affects versions 3.4.0 up to 3.4.2 and is mitigated by avoiding the scanning of untrusted content.
items.bottom_line: If you use Checkov to scan untrusted Terraform configurations, you must ensure external module downloading is disabled or the tool is updated to avoid internal network exposure.

items.title: On the hunt for ARTEX: understanding agentic attacks in AWS environments
items.one_liner: AI-native penetration framework ARTEX was observed actively exploiting compromised AWS credentials and public Cognito pools to hunt for financial data.
items.summary: Datadog Security Labs reported in-the-wild activity by ARTEX—an AI-native autonomous penetration framework developed by a Chinese creator—targeting AWS environments to harvest financial data and credentials in October 2026. Operating through hosted web consoles and LLM agent teams, ARTEX utilizes compromised long-term IAM access keys to search CloudWatch logs via FilterLogEvents and abuses public Amazon Cognito user pools for anonymous sign-ups and account enumeration. Originally published on GitHub in July 2026 and closed-source after surpassing 12,000 forks, the platform accepts API keys for multiple LLM providers such as OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Anthropic, dynamically switching providers if keys are revoked.
key_facts: Target platforms: AWS (CloudWatch, Cognito), Okta, Entra ID
Supported LLM providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Qwen
items.bottom_line: The AI-native exploitation framework ARTEX is actively weaponizing LLM agent teams against cloud environments and identity providers.

items.title: Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet
items.one_liner: Google and law enforcement dismantled the 1.3-million-device XCPE set-top box botnet and banned OEM Videostrong for preinstalling the malware.
items.summary: Google, alongside international partners and law enforcement agencies, dismantled the XCPE backdoor botnet, which had compromised more than 1.3 million set-top boxes. Investigators determined the backdoor was intentionally developed by Android OEM/ODM Videostrong Technology Co. for financial gain by renting access to criminal affiliates who installed modules for ad-fraud, data exfiltration, and residential proxies. Google severed ties with Videostrong, banned them from manufacturing certified Android devices, and executed legal takedowns of C2 domains that will disrupt access to over 10 million additional infected devices.
key_facts: Infected devices dismantled: More than 1.3 million
Additional compromised devices cut off: At least 10 million
items.bottom_line: Google has banned hardware manufacturer Videostrong and dismantled a massive 1.3-million-device set-top box botnet built directly into Android hardware.

items.title: A Series of Unauthenticated Events: Chained Exploitation of Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days
items.one_liner: This critical vulnerability chain highlights the ongoing risk of VPN appliances as entry points for credential theft and lateral movement.
items.summary: Threat actor UTA0576 exploited a zero-day vulnerability chain in Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) VPN appliances to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution. The chain included an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-104935), a file write vulnerability, and a privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-111357). The attacker extracted sensitive credentials, including LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys, while deleting logs to hide their tracks. Ivanti has released patches for these vulnerabilities, and forensic investigation is recommended for any ICS devices showing signs of lateral movement.
items.bottom_line: Organizations using Ivanti Connect Secure must ensure they are fully patched against the CVE-2026-111357 privilege escalation and CVE-2026-104935 RCE chain.

items.title: Mind the (Patch) Gap: Multiple Chinese Threat Actors Chain 0-day Exploits in Chrome & Windows
items.one_liner: Chinese APT groups are actively exploiting a patch gap between upstream Chromium fixes and browser releases via chained 0-days.
items.summary: Volexity detected spear-phishing campaigns in September 2026 by Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo targeting NGOs using a multi-stage exploit chain. The attacks abused reflected XSS on legitimate websites to redirect victims to a Google Chrome zero-day, CVE-2026-85046, which was unpatched in released browser versions despite upstream fixes in Chromium. The exploit chain leveraged a V8 type-confusion bug (CVE-2026-85046), a WebAssembly sandbox escape (CVE-2026-87491), and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880) to deploy malware including the GRIMWEDGE backdoor and SUPERSTOMP loader.
items.bottom_line: Threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo have been observed chaining a Chrome zero-day (CVE-2026-85046) and Windows kernel bug to target NGOs with persistent backdoors.

items.title: US military says it disabled merchant ship trying to breach Iran blockade
items.one_liner: The US military disabled a merchant vessel in the Gulf of Oman for allegedly violating the blockade on Iranian ports.

items.title: EXPOSURE: Explaining Sources of Uncertainty in Reinforcement Learning
items.one_liner: EXPOSURE uses a mask-aware belief network to explain both return uncertainty and belief uncertainty in reinforcement learning agents.
items.summary: Researchers proposed EXPOSURE, a framework using a single mask-aware belief network for both action selection and Shapley explanations to explain sources of uncertainty in reinforcement learning. The method explains the variance of the return by splitting it into an observational part due to missing features and an inherent part due to environment randomness, alongside the entropy of belief over masked features. Tested on tic-tac-toe and Minesweeper where exact Shapley values are computable, EXPOSURE provided more accurate explanations of expected return uncertainty while uniquely explaining belief uncertainty.
items.bottom_line: EXPOSURE advances reinforcement learning explainability by separating return variance into environmental and observational sources while quantifying belief entropy.

items.title: Why is RBI moving gold back to India? What Russia's frozen reserves and 1991 crisis reveal
items.one_liner: The RBI repatriated 60 tonnes of gold domestically in recent months, raising its local gold holdings to 84%.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India brought back roughly 60 tonnes of gold between April and September 2026, increasing domestic gold reserve holdings to approximately 84%. The RBI's half-yearly report shows domestic holdings reached 740.13 metric tonnes out of 880.52 total metric tonnes. While the central bank maintains that repatriating gold is part of routine reserve management and takes advantage of adequate domestic storage capacity, analysts note that the shift occurs amid growing global concerns over foreign asset safety following Western freezes of Russian reserves. This strategy starkly contrasts with India's 1991 economic crisis when emergency gold had to be leased and sold abroad.
items.bottom_line: Bringing gold back to domestic vaults enhances physical control and mitigates geopolitical risks associated with foreign asset storage.

items.one_liner: Sebi permits foreign portfolio investors to trade physically settled non-agri commodity derivatives like bullion starting June 2027 with strict delivery safeguards.
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) revised its commodity derivatives framework to allow foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to trade in physically settled non-agricultural commodity contracts starting June 1, 2027. Previously, FPI participation was restricted to cash-settled non-agricultural futures and indices such as crude oil and natural gas. Under the new rules, FPIs can trade bullion and base metals contracts but must exit or roll over open positions before the tender or staggered delivery period begins to avoid compulsory physical settlement. If FPIs fail to square off positions by the pre-specified cutoff, residual positions automatically transfer to designated trading or clearing members under a mandatory risk-absorption agreement.
items.bottom_line: SEBI is opening physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives to FPIs from June 2027, backed by mandatory position rollover and transfer rules.

items.one_liner: Temporal evaluation of LLMs for drug discovery shows that knowledge graphs often leak future trial data unless strictly managed.

items.title: SOLO: Towards Sample-Faithful and Detectable LLM Watermarking under Repeated Sampling via Content-Anchored Single-Owner Contexts
items.one_liner: SOLO is a new LLM watermarking approach that uses content-anchored single-owner contexts to prevent cross-response collisions during repeated sampling.
items.summary: Large language model providers frequently apply watermarks to generated outputs, but applications relying on repeated sampling for self-consistency and best-of-n selection create severe cross-response context collisions. Existing distortion-free watermarks deduplicate keyed contexts only within a single response, inadvertently coupling sibling responses from the same prompt and causing high collision rates. To solve this, researchers propose SOLO, a watermarking method that maintains a request-scoped context history while anchoring its keyed contexts on content selected via min-hash. This ensures that sibling responses rarely compete for contexts, allowing them to be jointly distributed as independent unwatermarked responses that remain independently detectable with a single key.
items.bottom_line: SOLO resolves LLM watermarking failures in repeated-sampling applications by anchoring contexts with min-hash, preserving self-consistency while maintaining detectability.

items.title: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
items.one_liner: PatternMiner combines LLM-guided dataset generation and narrow model interpretability to automate open-ended mathematical discovery and theorem proving.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced PatternMiner, an AI-driven framework that bridges text-based LLM reasoning with narrow machine learning models for automated mathematical discovery. PatternMiner directs an LLM agent to generate mathematical datasets based on initial broad queries, train narrow ML models, extract behavioral patterns using interpretability techniques, and formulate formal conjectures. The system then instructs the agent to search for counterexamples using mathematical software, iteratively refining the conjecture until it can be successfully proven. items.title: Aligned Machine: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Embedding Similarity via Human Comparative Judgements
items.one_liner: The Aligned Machine benchmark uses human preferences to evaluate semantic alignment in multimodal embedding models.
items.summary: Researchers introduced Aligned Machine, an interactive public platform that gathers human comparative judgments to generate a continuously growing Human-Aligned Similarity Benchmark (HASB) for multimodal embedding models. Findings show text-only models consistently achieve higher human agreement than multimodal models, with multimodal alignment performing best on image-image comparisons and worst on text-text comparisons. The framework is designed to track concept drift, bias, and domain-specific performance over time.
items.bottom_line: AI engineers auditing embedding models should leverage human-aligned comparative benchmarks to measure real semantic consistency.

items.title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration
items.one_liner: A massive systematic review of 2,289 studies highlights structural bottlenecks, evaluation gaps, and the dominance of hard-selection routing in conditional LLM architectures and agent workflows.
items.summary: A systematic review of 2,289 studies published between 2017 and September 2026 analyzes conditional computation methods across token-level gating, query-level model cascades, and task-level multi-agent coordination. The review synthesizes these works under a unified two-step inspect-then-allocate framework, revealing that discrete hard selection dominates the literature at 70%, 83%, and 91% for respective scales. Computational overhead emerges as a top operational bottleneck across every layer, while engineering safeguards remain sharply asymmetric with intra-layer gating favoring load balancing over uncertainty estimation. Meanwhile, publication volume accelerates fastest in agentic task delegation, where routing mechanisms are least often isolated experimentally and methodological bias risk is highest.
items.bottom_line: Conditional computation frameworks suffer from asymmetric safety guarantees and severe computational bottlenecks, with agentic delegation seeing the fastest publication growth but the highest bias risk.

items.title: Faster and Better Query (FBQ): Learning Future-Position Probes from the First Generated Token
items.one_liner: FBQ optimizes LLM cache management by using learned additive offsets from the first output token to approximate future decoding queries in a single forward pass.
items.summary: Researchers proposed Faster and Better Query (FBQ) to construct low-cost pseudo queries from the first generated token of large language models, addressing the challenge of evicting prompt keys and values without seeing subsequent queries. Instead of relying on a generic opening that fails to provide literal guesses for successive tokens, FBQ preserves the first embedding and learns an additive offset at each of the seven remaining positions. These offsets are trained to predict the average prompt attention of a full-cache continuation, and experiments on LongBench demonstrate that FBQ performs comparably to eight-step Lookahead Q-Cache using a single forward pass.
items.bottom_line: FBQ eliminates the need for expensive autoregressive draft steps when evicting prompt caches by predicting future attention with learned token offsets.

items.title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
items.one_liner: MindGuard2 provides a high-performance, low-latency reasoning guard model built on a clinically grounded taxonomy for mental health safety.

items.title: Budget, Readout or Reasoning? Where Small Reasoning Models Lose Value in Auction Bidding
items.one_liner: Small reasoning models often underperform in auction bidding due to internal bias and premature reasoning termination, but can be corrected with simple audit layers.
items.summary: A study evaluating small reasoning models (4B-14B parameters) in auction bidding scenarios reveals that these models often fail to select the optimal bid despite correctly ranking options in their reasoning traces. items.bottom_line: For automated bidding agents, the reasoning trace is more reliable than the final output; auditing the trace against the output is essential for performance.

items.title: SlicePlanner: Logic-Guided Agentic AI for Online QoS-Aware Network Slicing in Open RAN

items.title: REFORGE: LLM-Assisted RTL Bug Repair with Structured Context and Verification Feedback
items.one_liner: REFORGE provides a multi-stage, evidence-accumulating framework for LLM-assisted RTL bug repair that verifies functionality, equivalence, and security.

items.title: Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models via Agentic Model Editing
items.one_liner: Agentic Model Editing enables LLM agents to dynamically design custom few-shot adaptation programs for vision-language models.
items.summary: Few-shot adaptation of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) typically relies on pre-specified procedures to fit prompts or classifiers. To overcome domain-specific visual differences, researchers propose Agentic Model Editing (AME), an agentic framework that dynamically designs input transformations, encoder edits, and feature computations as executable adaptation programs. The LLM agent inspects images, class semantics, and model parameters to formulate and test candidate programs on a support set using validation accuracy for selection. Evaluated across eleven datasets with CLIP ViT-B/16, AME achieves average accuracies of 81.2% without back-propagation and 81.9% with back-propagation.
items.bottom_line: Agentic Model Editing (AME) allows an LLM agent to construct domain-customized adaptation programs for Vision-Language Models without relying on pre-specified procedures.

claims.text: Across eleven datasets with CLIP ViT-B/16, AME achieves the highest average accuracies of 81.2% without back-propagation and 81.9% with back-propagation among the compared methods.

items.title: Constraint-Aware Test-Time Scoring for LLM and VLM Candidate Selection
items.one_liner: A new scoring framework for LLMs improves output safety and correctness by integrating hard, grounded checks into the candidate selection process.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed a new scoring framework for LLM and VLM candidate selection that combines hard safety/correctness checks with soft-factor weighting. The method uses a drafting model to generate candidates, a configuration model to select checks, and scoring models to evaluate properties that cannot be computed by tools. Ablation studies show that hard checks are the primary driver of performance gains, particularly in improving code-generation safety and retrieval-augmented QA accuracy.
items.bottom_line: For production LLM pipelines, implementing grounded hard checks is more effective for safety and correctness than relying on soft-factor configuration or model confidence.

items.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
items.one_liner: AutoformBench evaluates AI models on formalizing advanced mathematics and building missing Lean infrastructure.
items.summary: AutoformBench is a new benchmark featuring 341 Lean 4 formalization tasks sourced from 24 advanced mathematical domains. Unlike traditional evaluations that present isolated theorem statements with existing Mathlib support, AutoformBench embeds problems within broader mathematical developments where agents must translate informal proofs into Lean while constructing missing definitions and intermediate lemmas. Evaluations of frontier models reveal a shared difficulty frontier where performance depends primarily on an agent's ability to build missing formal infrastructure rather than the specific mathematical domain.
items.bottom_line: AutoformBench introduces 341 Lean 4 formalization tasks that test an AI agent's ability to construct missing formal definitions and lemmas for advanced mathematics.

items.title: JOVE ICE: Intent Guided Cloud Edge Device Collaboration for AI Glasses
items.one_liner: JOVE ICE optimizes AI glasses performance by intelligently routing tasks between device, edge, and cloud based on user intent.
items.summary: JOVE ICE is a new collaborative framework designed for AI glasses that routes tasks between the glasses, a paired smartphone, and cloud servers based on user intent. By using hierarchical intent classification, the framework handles simple device control tasks locally on the glasses, reducing latency and token usage. Evaluations show a 13% reduction in time-to-first-token and an 11% decrease in token consumption compared to traditional cloud-heavy architectures.
items.bottom_line: Intent-aware task routing is a viable strategy for improving the efficiency and responsiveness of wearable AI devices.

items.title: EGSE: Evidence-Grounded Skill Evolution for Medical Reasoning Agents

items.title: Controllable CAD Generation and Interactive Editing of Fluid Rotors
items.one_liner: VaneCraft provides an agent-driven, unified CAD generation and editing framework specifically tailored for fluid machinery rotors.
items.summary: VaneCraft is a new agent-driven framework designed to automate CAD generation, inverse recovery, and interactive editing for rotors in fluid rotating machinery. The system utilizes a unified analytical representation that maps design controls to blade surfaces via an anisotropic partial differential equation, paired with a geometric parameter correction module using a joint geometric encoder and parameter decoder. Experiments indicate that VaneCraft successfully handles anisotropy control and parameter editing, outperforming existing representative baselines.
items.bottom_line: Rotor design in fluid machinery can be unified and controlled through agent-driven analytical representations and anisotropic partial differential equations.

items.title: MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents
items.one_liner: MedSkill-E2 targets the 'Enable But Underuse' gap in medical LLM agents, using execution feedback to drastically improve autonomous skill application.
items.summary: Researchers have identified a phenomenon termed skill Enable But Underuse, where LLM agents fail to apply specified rules and procedures effectively during autonomous execution despite having access to necessary skills. This limitation is critical in medical domains, where missing a single constraint results in incorrect outcomes. To address this, the authors introduce MedSkill-E2 and EBU-Bench, showing that evaluated models exhibit a mean skill-use accuracy gap of 43.94 percentage points. They propose EBU-Evolve, a method that uses execution feedback to refine skills and improve autonomous execution accuracy across models.
key_facts: Mean EBU gap: 43.94 percentage points on EBU-Bench
Accuracy improvement from EBU-Evolve: 33.33 to 55.17 percentage points improvement in autonomous execution
items.bottom_line: Medical LLM agents frequently suffer from skill Enable But Underuse gaps, which can be mitigated by EBU-Evolve feedback refinement.

items.title: Can Its Own Misses Teach an MLLM to Find Small Brain Metastases?
items.one_liner: LANTERN enables MLLMs to autonomously improve small brain metastasis detection by learning recursively from their own diagnostic misses.
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) struggle to locate small medical abnormalities like brain metastases. To address this, researchers introduced LANTERN (Lesion-finding AgeNt Through Error-driven Recursive leaRning), an error-driven loop where an MLLM recursively improves from its own misses through a failure census and an LLM mentor. Over 15 unattended rounds, LANTERN improved a fine-tuned 4B MLLM's detection rate from 75% to 94% of lesions on BraTS-MET at one false positive per scan, while maintaining high performance on external cohorts and unseen meningiomas. This demonstrates that an MLLM's own misses can successfully drive reliable recursive self-improvement in medical imaging tasks.
items.bottom_line: LANTERN uses an error-driven recursive learning loop to significantly boost MLLM detection rates for small brain metastases without relying on manual trial-and-error fine-tuning.

items.title: PeerReveal: Learning to Generalize in AI Peer Review Detection
items.one_liner: PeerReveal reliably detects AI-generated academic peer reviews by analyzing claim relationships and leveraging adversarial training.
items.summary: PeerReveal is an advanced AI peer review detector that combines learned relationships between review claims and reference claims with review-level textual signals to identify fully AI-generated reviews or AI-rewritten text. Evaluated on the PeerShift test set containing 5,430 reviews across diverse disciplines, the standard model achieves a pooled Macro-F1 score of 70.52%. Furthermore, an adversarial training framework using a local generator raises the pooled Macro-F1 score to 82.40%.
items.bottom_line: Robust detection of AI-assisted peer review requires examining granular claim-level dependencies combined with adversarial training against specialized local generators.

items.title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
items.one_liner: EATS improves tool selection and reasoning for medical AI agents by leveraging accumulated test-time interaction experiences.
items.summary: Medical reasoning agents combine LLM reasoning with specialized neural tools, but general-purpose LLMs lack training exposure to clinical tools, making tool selection challenging due to output uncertainty and distributional shifts. To address this, researchers propose EATS (Experience-Augmented Tool Selection), a strategy that constructs a memory of past interactions—including queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback—without requiring ground-truth supervision. By retrieving relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries, EATS scales naturally with test-time experience. Evaluations across four public datasets and three multimodal LLMs (including Qwen3-VL and GPT-5.5) show consistent performance gains in medical reasoning tasks.
key_facts: Evaluated datasets: ChestAgentBench, CheXbench, MIMIC-CXR, SLAKE-VQA
items.bottom_line: EATS enhances medical reasoning agents by utilizing an experience-augmented memory of past tool interactions to guide tool selection without ground-truth supervision.

items.title: General-Purpose Decision Models for AI Configuration Tuning
items.one_liner: Evaluating whether general-purpose decision models can improve AI configuration tuning over conventional optimizers.
items.summary: Researchers investigated whether general-purpose decision models like Jev can guide AI configuration tuning by comparing them against conventional optimizers, performance predictors, and region guiders across eight tasks. Conventional optimizers and established predictors outperformed Jev in rank and prediction accuracy in six and seven out of eight comparisons respectively. However, Jev successfully served as a region guider, finding configurations with lower perplexity than native tuners at the cost of increased decision time and API fees. These findings highlight practical trade-offs for developers when selecting decision strategies and balancing quality against tuning costs.

items.title: ExtractBench Pro: The Long Tail of Document Extraction
items.one_liner: ExtractBench Pro evaluates document extraction tools, finding that top coding agents outperform specialized APIs on accuracy but at higher computational costs.
items.summary: Researchers introduced ExtractBench Pro, a schema-guided benchmark designed to test six challenging document extraction modes using synthetic document generators. While frontier coding agents like Claude Code Opus 5.5 and Codex GPT-6 Astra outperformed specialized APIs in accuracy and Value F1, they incurred higher execution costs per page. The benchmark highlights persistent failures in applying document-specific definitions and recovering relational data from diagrams.

items.summary: Hugging Face published an educational blog series exploring how to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems using small, affordable language models. items.one_liner: Interviews with 17 scientists reveal that AI agents in research require strict verification frameworks encompassing validation, privacy, and accountability.
items.summary: A qualitative study by Hugging Face researchers interviewing 17 natural, applied, and social scientists highlights critical governance and ethical requirements for deploying autonomous AI agents in scientific research. items.title: icsScanner: Safe Active Vulnerability Scanning for ICS and OT Networks
items.one_liner: icsScanner is an active vulnerability scanner designed specifically for ICS and OT networks with strict pre-probe fingerprinting and safety gates.
items.summary: Industrial control systems (ICS) and operational technology (OT) environments present unique scanning risks where active probes can crash fragile twenty-year-old programmable logic controllers (PLCs). To address this domain gap, security researchers developed icsScanner, an active vulnerability scanner built specifically for OT networks. The tool implements safety guardrails by fingerprinting targets before every probe, enforcing global and per-target rate limiting, and capping confidence levels based strictly on evidentiary support. It covers 250 checks across 29 protocol families, including Modbus, S7comm, OPC UA, PROFINET, and DNP3, while maintaining strict architectural separation to prevent physical safety risks.

items.bottom_line: Standard IT vulnerability scanners risk causing physical shutdowns in critical infrastructure, requiring dedicated OT tools with strict pre-check fingerprinting and rate limiting.

items.title: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery
items.one_liner: GPT-6.2 Astra demonstrated advanced research capabilities by autonomously identifying the author of a 200-year-old anonymous sketchbook.
items.summary: Historian Mark Humphries successfully used GPT-6.2 Astra to identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library. The AI autonomously cross-referenced primary and secondary sources, including a obscure diary entry, to link the work to the vicomte de Chabot in just 22 minutes. This case study demonstrates the potential for agentic AI systems to perform complex historical research tasks that previously required extensive human labor. While some experts suggest this may lead to a 'crisis of confidence' in historical methodology, others argue that the interpretive nature of history remains a uniquely human endeavor.
items.bottom_line: Agentic AI is now capable of performing high-level historical research, potentially shifting the role of historians from data gathering to higher-level interpretation.

items.title: Node.js 27 Alpha Adds HTTP Security Protections and Deprecates TLS 1.2 Renegotiation
items.one_liner: Node.js 27 alpha introduces critical connection reuse fixes and opt-out controls for deprecated TLS 1.2 renegotiation ahead of future defaults.
items.summary: The Node.js project released version 27.0.0-alpha.0.2.0, introducing HTTP security protections and new controls for TLS 1.2 renegotiation. The build carries forward a fix for CVE-2026-105481, an HTTP client connection reuse flaw where responses could be improperly matched to pre-arrival data. It also allows developers to explicitly disable TLS 1.2 renegotiation by setting allowRenegotiation to false, preceding a future default disablement. Additionally, the update enforces maxSessionMemory limits for client requests on HTTP/2 streams and refines connection pooling behavior for HTTPS.
key_facts: CVE-2026-105481: HTTP client connection reuse vulnerability
items.bottom_line: Node.js 27 alpha lets developers test disabling TLS 1.2 renegotiation while carrying fixes for connection reuse and memory limit vulnerabilities.

Because physical gold is expensive, retail investors are weighing gold ETFs against gold mutual funds. Market experts note that gold ETFs offer lower costs since they do not carry the expense ratios or exit loads charged by mutual fund managers who act as funds of funds. Consequently, well-informed investors and traders are advised to utilize gold ETFs with low trading premiums, while less-informed investors may opt for gold mutual funds.

items.title: Monitoring the Paper Machine: AI Research in the Age of Acceleration

As authors, reviewers, and area chairs delegate more of their work to AI, conferences—and more generally the research field—gradually become an “AI system” in its own right. We call this evolving system, from individual conferences to the field as a whole, the “Paper Machine”. AI may accelerate its output beyond human capacity to understand or check it, while the incentives shaping that output may favour proxies for progress over progress itself. Monitoring this Paper Machine therefore requires tracking not only how much research is produced, but also how it is produced, presented, and evaluated.
